Old title: "Joint-loop equivalence: all_paths_via_even_odd linear vs non-linear (naive)" (kind: equiv-pair; algorithm: naive).

Prior classification and evidence in the retired corpus: valid, by a hand-written Lean kernel certificate (direct Lean kernel proof of the joint-loop equivalence using exact finite-path semantics for both even/odd iterations and the all-paths union recurrence; no external FOL assumptions). The retired corpus records this case among the twelve valid, conjecturally FO-obstructed cases (no archived Vampire refutation for this particular case). That kernel certificate is not carried into this corpus; the classification here is unknown until re-certified.

The command is not hand-authored: `Fidelity/Example0133.lean` states the two Datalog programs written for this case, compiles each with `Datalog.WhielCompiler.Naive`, writes the two compiled commands one after the other, renames the generated snapshots to the auxiliary input names `X_aux`, and proves the result equal to `inputCmd` by `decide +kernel`; the same module fixes `inputPre` and `inputPost` and pins the single loop `Hoare.preprocess` computes from the sequence. The two programs are independent, so the preprocessor merges them into the flag-free guarded parallel form.

The retired file's loop iterated destructively, carrying a second copy `SaX` of each relation and stepping the immediate-consequence operator from the empty relation; the compiled form accumulates, `T := T ∪ T_P(T)`, and reaches the same least fixpoint. The retired postcondition `(TaX = TaY) ∧ ((TbX = TbY) ∧ (TcX = TcY))` was stated over those previous-round copies, which equal the fixpoints at loop exit; the same equalities are stated here over the compiled output relations, so the triple says the same thing. The schema loses the copies `SaX`, `SbX`, `ScX`, `SaY`, `SbY`, `ScY` and gains the compiler's snapshots `TaX_aux`, `TbX_aux`, `TcX_aux`, `TaY_aux`, `TbY_aux`, `TcY_aux`. The precondition `true` is unchanged, and the expected verdict stays valid.
title: All paths via odd/even paths: linear versus non-linear program (two compiled loops)
explanation: The command runs two independently compiled Datalog programs in sequence — a linear even/odd program producing TaX, TbX and their union TcX, and a non-linear even/odd program producing TaY, TbY and their union TcY — merged by the preprocessor into a single verified loop. The postcondition states that all three pairs of relations agree, TaX=TaY, TbX=TbY and TcX=TcY, so the Hoare triple is an equivalence claim between the linear and non-linear implementations of the even/odd path decomposition and its union (all paths of length one or more), both reaching the same least fixpoints.
preInWords: The precondition is simply true, imposing no constraint on the input relations.
postInWords: The postcondition asserts that the linear program's three outputs equal the non-linear program's corresponding outputs: TaX = TaY, TbX = TbY, and TcX = TcY.

datalog.label: programX — Odd and even paths and their union, linearly.
datalog.text:
TbX(x1, y1) :- E(x1, y1).
TbX(x1, y1) :- E(x1, z1), TaX(z1, y1).
TaX(x1, y1) :- E(x1, z1), TbX(z1, y1).
TcX(x1, y1) :- TaX(x1, y1).
TcX(x1, y1) :- TbX(x1, y1).

TaY(x1, y1) :- TaY(x1, z1), TaY(z1, y1).
TaY(x1, y1) :- TbY(x1, z1), TbY(z1, y1).
TbY(x1, y1) :- E(x1, y1).
TbY(x1, y1) :- TbY(x1, z1), TaY(z1, y1).
TbY(x1, y1) :- TaY(x1, z1), TbY(z1, y1).
TcY(x1, y1) :- TaY(x1, y1).
TcY(x1, y1) :- TbY(x1, y1).
